description: Internal metrics of the oteldb storage engine (github.com/oteldb/storage): ingest admission, flush, merge and part shape, fetch, cluster RPC failover and the object-store backend. Note: the engine's PromQL has no histogram_quantile, so latency panels show sum/count means alongside the raw bucket rates.

panels.description: Nodes publishing storage-engine metrics (storage.cluster.self_absent is recorded by every node).
panels.title: Nodes reporting

panels.description: storage.cluster.self_absent — the node is up and serving but missing from etcd, so no peer routes anything to it. Should be 0.
panels.title: Nodes absent from member set

panels.description: storage.disk.out_of_space — an engine is refusing writes because the medium is out of bytes or inodes. Should be 0.
panels.title: Engines out of disk space

panels.description: storage.parts.total summed over the selected nodes and signals.
panels.title: Flushed parts

panels.description: storage.parts.merge_backlog — unsealed parts a merge may still take.
panels.title: Merge backlog

panels.description: storage.fetch.total rate.
panels.title: Fetches/s

panels.description: storage.ingest.accepted — points accepted for storage, counted at the engine that stores them.
panels.title: Accepted points/s

panels.description: Admission control. storage.ingest.rejected (by reason), storage.ingest.sampled_dropped and storage.ingest.overflowed. Nothing is charted until admission actually sheds — an empty panel is the healthy state.
panels.title: Shed points/s

panels.description: storage.wal.appends / fsyncs / rotations. Only appends is exercised by the dev stack; fsyncs and rotations need a WAL configured with durability and enough volume to roll a segment.
panels.title: WAL activity

panels.description: storage.flush.total — head flushes to an immutable part.
panels.title: Flushes/s

panels.description: storage.flush.duration_sum / _count. The engine's PromQL has no histogram_quantile, so this is a mean, not a quantile — read it next to the bucket panel.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.flush.duration_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.flush.duration_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean flush duration

panels.description: Rate of storage.flush.duration_bucket per cumulative le bucket (seconds). Buckets are the OTel defaults, so the useful signal is which bucket stops growing.
panels.title: Flush duration distribution

panels.description: storage.flush.rows_sum rate — rows landing in parts.
panels.title: Rows flushed/s

panels.description: storage.flush.rows_sum / _count — how big a head gets before it is cut.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.flush.rows_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.flush.rows_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean rows per flush

panels.description: storage.disk.rejected_writes — writes the medium could not store. Empty is healthy; a non-zero rate means the node is acking writes it cannot keep.
panels.title: Disk-pressure rejections/s

panels.description: storage.merge.total — background merges (compaction/retention/downsample/recompress).
panels.title: Merges/s

panels.description: storage.merge.duration_sum / _count.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.merge.duration_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.merge.duration_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean merge duration

panels.description: storage.merge.parts_in_sum / _count. Near the minimum fan-in means the selector is merging pairs and never catching up.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.merge.parts_in_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.merge.parts_in_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean source parts per merge

panels.description: storage.parts.total against storage.parts.sealed. Sealed parts are at the merge cap and no merge reconsiders them, so total minus sealed is the part count compaction can still reduce.
panels.title: Parts

panels.description: storage.parts.merge_backlog (unsealed parts a merge may still take) and storage.parts.merge_candidates (what the next merge would select). A backlog that only grows means compaction is losing.
panels.title: Merge backlog & candidates

panels.description: storage.merge.cap_bytes — the part size at which a merged part is sealed.
panels.title: Seal threshold

panels.description: storage.fetch.total.
panels.title: Fetches/s

panels.description: storage.fetch.duration_sum / _count.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.duration_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.duration_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean fetch duration

panels.description: Rate of storage.fetch.duration_bucket per cumulative le bucket (seconds).
panels.title: Fetch duration distribution

panels.description: storage.fetch.series_matched_sum / _count — index selectivity.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.series_matched_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.series_matched_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean series matched per fetch

panels.description: storage.fetch.rows_returned_sum / _count.

targets.expr:
sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.rows_returned_sum", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (signal) (rate({"storage.fetch.rows_returned_count", "host.name"=~"$node", signal=~"$signal"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean rows returned per fetch

panels.description: storage.fetch.parts_scanned is the read amplification the merge backlog buys you. storage.fetch.decode_budget_forced_admissions counts queries let past the decode-memory ceiling after a stalled wait — any non-zero rate means the ceiling is not holding.
panels.title: Parts scanned/s & forced admissions

panels.description: storage.rpc.attempts — every node-to-node transport attempt, including the first, by op.
panels.title: RPC attempts/s

panels.description: storage.rpc.retries (sequential retry) and storage.rpc.hedges (opportunistic concurrent attempt because the in-flight one was slow). A rising rate localizes a degrading peer or link.
panels.title: Retries & hedges/s

panels.description: storage.rpc.shard_absent: this node owns the shard in the ring but holds no data, so the read failed over — the ring and the data disagree. storage.rpc.shard_incomplete: it holds the shard but came back without the unflushed head, so the window is only on another owner. A sustained incomplete rate means nobody is flushing.
panels.title: Shard failover/s

panels.description: storage.cluster.self_absent stands at 1 while a node is running but missing from the member set; storage.cluster.rejoins counts re-registrations after a lost lease. A node flapping here looks perfectly healthy from every other signal.
panels.title: Membership

panels.description: storage.backend.ops by op and result.
panels.title: Backend ops/s

panels.description: storage.backend.ops with result != ok. not_found is normal for probe reads and deletes; a sustained error rate is not.
panels.title: Backend non-ok ops/s

panels.description: storage.backend.bytes by op.
panels.title: Backend throughput

panels.description: storage.backend.latency_sum / _count by op.
panels.title: Mean backend latency

panels.description: Rate of storage.backend.latency_bucket per cumulative le bucket (seconds).
panels.title: Backend latency distribution

panels.description: go.memory.used by memory class.
panels.title: Go memory used

panels.description: go.goroutine.count.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: go.memory.allocated rate — allocator pressure, the input to GC frequency.
panels.title: Allocation rate

panels.description: go.memory.gc.goal — the heap size the next GC cycle targets.
panels.title: Heap goal

panels.description: odbingest.otlp.requests — OTLP requests reaching the split-process writer.
panels.title: OTLP requests/s

panels.description: odbingest.otlp.items — points, spans and log records decoded.
panels.title: OTLP items/s

panels.description: odbingest.otlp.decoded_bytes.
panels.title: OTLP decoded bytes/s

panels.description: odbingest.cluster.accepted_points — what odbingest handed to the storage ring.
panels.title: Points accepted by the cluster/s

list.description: Telemetry signal the engine instance holds.
list.label: signal
list.name: signal

title: storage: engine
